message.content: {"caption":"A boxed prompt instructs a main agent to delegate problem-solving work to sub-agents and coordinate their efforts.","description":"A single rounded rectangular text panel has a dark charcoal-teal header labeled “Main Agent Prompt” and a light gray body of monospaced text. The body introduces a problem statement placeholder, “{problem_statement},” between start and end markers. It tells the main agent to delegate the problem to as many sub-agents as needed, relay it accurately, and usually avoid repeating a long statement verbatim; instead, give clear directions and let sub-agents refer to the statement. It says file- and directory-viewing tools are provided to help the main agent understand context and direct sub-agents, but the main agent is only a router, delegator, and orchestrator, not equipped to do substantive work. It instructs the agent to consult the listed tools available to sub-agents when deciding whom to call next, and says sub-agents are responsible for making the necessary state changes. There are no arrows, other connections, marks, or plotted data.","figure_type":"other","chart_values":[]}
